questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: She ___ to school every day.
questions.explanation: A habitual action with a singular subject takes the simple present with -s: goes.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: They ___ cricket when it started to rain.
questions.explanation: An action in progress in the past, interrupted by another past action, uses the past continuous: were playing.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: I ___ this book twice already.
questions.explanation: An action completed before now, with 'already', takes the present perfect: have read.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: By the time we reached the station, the train ___.
questions.explanation: The train left before another past event (we reached), so the past perfect had left is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: She ___ in Jaipur since 2015.
questions.explanation: 'Since' with a point in time and an action continuing to now needs the present perfect: has lived.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Verbs of state such as know, have (possess), understand and belong are not normally used in the continuous form.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Rewrite in the simple past tense: 'My uncle visits us every summer.'
questions.answer: My uncle visited us every summer.
questions.explanation: The simple past of a regular verb is formed by adding -ed.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Fill in the blank with the correct form of the verb in brackets: 'By next June, I ___ (complete) my course.'
keyPoints: action finished before a future time
questions.explanation: 'By next June' marks a future deadline, so the future perfect is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The children ___ playing in the garden.
questions.explanation: 'Children' is plural, so the plural verb 'are' is needed.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Each of the girls ___ a prize.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so it takes 'has'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: A number of students ___ absent today.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' means 'several' and takes a plural verb: are.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The number of students in our school ___ increased.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' is singular, so it takes 'has'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.
questions.explanation: Names of subjects ending in -s, such as mathematics, are singular.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: One of the books on the shelf ___ torn.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'One', not 'books', so the singular verb 'is' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Correct the error: 'The furniture in these rooms are old.'
questions.answer: The furniture in these rooms is old.
keyPoints: it takes a singular verb: is
questions.explanation: Furniture is uncountable and singular in grammar.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Why do we say 'The police have arrived' and not 'The police has arrived'?
questions.answer: 'Police' is a collective noun that is always treated as plural in English, so it takes a plural verb.
questions.explanation: The word 'police' refers to a group of officers and always takes a plural verb.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct article: She is ___ honest girl.
questions.explanation: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound because the h is silent, so 'an' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct article: My brother is studying at ___ university in Delhi.
questions.explanation: 'University' begins with a 'yoo' consonant sound, so 'a' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct article: ___ Ganga is a sacred river in India.
questions.explanation: Names of rivers take the definite article: the Ganga.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: We have ___ time; the film starts in two minutes.
questions.explanation: 'Time' is uncountable, and 'little' means hardly any, which fits the sense of shortage.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: Neena has two cousins. ___ of them live in Pune.
questions.explanation: 'Both' refers to two people together and takes a plural verb.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: He plays the cricket every evening.
I had a breakfast at eight.
The sun rises in the east.
questions.explanation: 'The' is used with the sun and with directions; games and meals take no article here, and 'European' needs 'a'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Fill in with a, an or the: 'I saw ___ owl on the roof. ___ owl was very big.'
keyPoints: 'an' before the vowel sound in owl
questions.explanation: The first mention takes an indefinite article; the second mention is specific, so 'the'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain why we say 'an hour' but 'a university'.
questions.answer: The choice of a or an depends on the sound, not the spelling. 'Hour' begins with a vowel sound because the h is silent, while 'university' begins with a consonant 'yoo' sound.
keyPoints: hour starts with a vowel sound
university starts with a consonant sound
questions.explanation: 'An' goes before vowel sounds and 'a' before consonant sounds.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: The cat jumped ___ the wall.
questions.explanation: 'Over' shows movement across the top of something.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: I have been waiting for you ___ morning.
questions.explanation: 'Since' marks the starting point of a continuing action in the present perfect continuous.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: She is afraid ___ spiders.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'afraid' is followed by the preposition 'of'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: The meeting was postponed ___ heavy rain.
questions.explanation: 'Because of' is followed by a noun phrase; 'because' needs a full clause.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: He was tired, ___ he kept working.
questions.explanation: 'Yet' shows contrast between being tired and continuing to work.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: Hurry up, ___ you will miss the bus.
questions.explanation: 'Or' (meaning otherwise) joins a command to its warning of consequence.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Join the sentences using 'although': 'It was raining. We went for a walk.'
questions.answer: Although it was raining, we went for a walk.
questions.explanation: 'Although' joins two ideas that contrast with each other.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the difference between 'beside' and 'besides' with one sentence for each.
questions.answer: 'Beside' means next to: She sat beside me. 'Besides' means in addition to: Besides English, she speaks French.
questions.explanation: The two words look alike but have different meanings.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: You ___ obey your teachers.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses duty or obligation.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ I borrow your pen, please?
questions.explanation: 'May' is used to ask permission politely.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: She ___ swim when she was five.
questions.explanation: 'Could' is the past form of 'can' for ability in the past.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: You ___ not touch the wires; they are live.
questions.explanation: 'Must not' expresses a strong prohibition because of danger.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ to finish my homework before dinner.
questions.explanation: 'To' follows 'have' to express necessity: have to.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is a polite request?
options: Could you please pass the salt?
questions.explanation: 'Could you please...?' is the polite, question form of a request.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Rewrite using 'ought to': 'You should respect your elders.'
questions.answer: You ought to respect your elders.
keyPoints: base form of the verb follows
questions.explanation: 'Ought to' is similar in meaning to 'should' and is followed by the base verb.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the difference in meaning between 'He may come' and 'He must come'.
questions.answer: 'He may come' says it is possible that he will come. 'He must come' says it is necessary or compulsory for him to come.
questions.explanation: Different modal verbs express different attitudes of the speaker.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'The boy kicked the ball.'
options: The ball is kicked by the boy.
The ball was kicked by the boy.
The ball has been kicked by the boy.
questions.explanation: Simple past active becomes 'was/were + past participle' in the passive.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'They are building a bridge.'
options: A bridge is being built by them.
A bridge was built by them.
A bridge is built by them.
A bridge has been built by them.
questions.explanation: Present continuous becomes 'is/are being + past participle'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the active voice of: 'The letter was written by Meera.'
questions.explanation: 'Was written' is simple past passive, so the active is simple past: wrote.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The thief ___ by the police yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' needs a past tense; the passive past is 'was caught'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: English ___ in many countries.
questions.explanation: A general fact in the passive uses 'is/are + past participle'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence cannot be changed into the passive voice?
questions.explanation: 'Sleeps' is intransitive and has no object, so there is nothing to become the subject of a passive sentence.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into the passive voice: 'The teacher will announce the results tomorrow.'
questions.answer: The results will be announced by the teacher tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Simple future passive is 'will be + past participle'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into the passive voice: 'Who wrote this letter?'
questions.answer: By whom was this letter written?
questions.explanation: Questions with 'who' change to 'by whom' in the passive.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I am tired.'
options: He said that he was tired.
He said that I am tired.
He said that he has been tired.
He said that I was tired.
questions.explanation: The pronoun 'I' becomes 'he' and the present tense changes to the past: was.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said, 'I will call you tomorrow.'
options: She said that she will call me the next day.
She said that she called me the next day.
She said that she would call me the next day.
She said that she would call you the next day.
questions.explanation: Will changes to would, 'I' to 'she', 'you' to 'me', and 'tomorrow' to 'the next day'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He asked, 'Where do you live?'
options: He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where do you live.
He asked me that where I lived.
He asked me where I lived.
questions.explanation: In reported questions the word order becomes that of a statement and the tense moves back.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She asked, 'Do you like tea?'
options: She asked me that I liked tea.
She asked me if I liked tea.
She asked me do I like tea.
She asked me what I liked tea.
questions.explanation: Yes/no questions are reported with 'if' or 'whether', in statement order.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: Mother said to me, 'Don't touch the stove.'
options: Mother told me that don't touch the stove.
Mother said me not to touch the stove.
Mother told me not to touch the stove.
Mother told me do not touch the stove.
questions.explanation: A negative command is reported with 'told ... not to + verb'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: Rita said, 'Alas! I have lost my watch.'
options: Rita exclaimed with sorrow that she had lost her watch.
Rita exclaimed with sorrow that she has lost her watch.
Rita exclaimed with sorrow that I had lost my watch.
Rita exclaimed with sorrow that she would lose her watch.
questions.explanation: An exclamation is reported with 'exclaimed with sorrow that'; the present perfect becomes the past perfect and the pronouns change.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into direct speech: Arun said that he was going to Mumbai the next day.
questions.answer: Arun said, 'I am going to Mumbai tomorrow.'
questions.explanation: Reverse the changes of tense, pronoun and time expression.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said to the class, 'Why are you making so much noise?'
questions.answer: The teacher asked the class why they were making so much noise.
keyPoints: statement word order, no question mark
you becomes they, are making becomes were making
questions.explanation: A wh-question is reported with the same question word, in statement order.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: In 'I know that he is honest', the clause 'that he is honest' is a ___ clause.
questions.explanation: The clause is the object of 'know', so it does the work of a noun.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which complex sentence can be made from 'He worked hard. He failed.'?
options: He worked hard and he failed.
Because he worked hard, he failed.
He failed, so he worked hard.
Although he worked hard, he failed.
questions.explanation: 'Although' correctly shows the contrast between working hard and failing.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Rewrite with 'so ... that': 'She is too weak to walk.'
options: She is so weak that she can walk.
She is so weak that she could walk.
She is weak enough to walk.
She is so weak that she cannot walk.
questions.explanation: 'Too ... to' has a negative sense, which becomes 'so ... that ... cannot'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence has the same meaning as 'Mount Everest is higher than any other mountain in the world'?
options: Mount Everest is as high as any other mountain.
No other mountain in the world is as high as Mount Everest.
Some mountains are as high as Mount Everest.
Mount Everest is the lowest mountain in the world.
questions.explanation: The positive degree says that no other mountain equals Everest in height.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which of these is a compound sentence?
options: Because it rained, we stayed home.
The boy who sits there is my cousin.
I wanted to go, but it was late.
Although she was ill, she came.
questions.explanation: A compound sentence joins two independent clauses with a coordinating conjunction such as 'but'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence contains an adverb clause of time?
options: When the bell rang, the students left.
The students left and the bell rang.
The students who were late left.
questions.explanation: 'When the bell rang' tells us the time of the action and cannot stand alone.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Rewrite using 'as soon as': 'No sooner had she reached home than it started to rain.'
questions.answer: As soon as she reached home, it started to rain.
keyPoints: as soon as replaces no sooner ... than
past simple tense in both parts
questions.explanation: Both patterns say that one event followed immediately after the other.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Combine into one sentence using a relative pronoun: 'I met a girl. She had won a medal.'
questions.answer: I met a girl who had won a medal.
keyPoints: second sentence becomes an adjective clause
questions.explanation: 'Who' replaces 'she' and joins the two sentences.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: An exclamation begins with a capital letter and ends with an exclamation mark.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
questions.explanation: 'Girl's' shows possession by one girl; the other sentences misuse the apostrophe.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
options: Riya bought apples, oranges and bananas.
Riya bought, apples, oranges and bananas.
Riya bought apples oranges, and, bananas.
Riya bought apples, oranges and, bananas.
questions.explanation: Commas separate items in a list, with 'and' joining the last two.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: He asked, Where are you going?
questions.explanation: A comma introduces the quotation, which begins with a capital letter and ends with its own question mark inside the quotes.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence uses the semicolon correctly?
options: I wanted to play; however, it was raining.
I wanted to play, however it was raining.
I wanted to play; however it was raining;
I wanted; to play, however, it was raining.
questions.explanation: A semicolon can join two related independent clauses, with a comma after 'however'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence correctly shows that the speaker is inviting Grandma to eat?
questions.explanation: A comma before a name addressed directly separates the person spoken to from the rest of the sentence.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Punctuate correctly: the teacher said open your books to page ten
questions.answer: The teacher said, 'Open your books to page ten.'
keyPoints: capital letters at the start of the sentence and the quotation
inverted commas and a full stop
questions.explanation: Direct speech is enclosed in inverted commas and introduced by a comma.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the difference in meaning between 'The students, who were tired, left early' and 'The students who were tired left early'.
questions.answer: With commas, all the students were tired and all left early. Without commas, only the students who were tired left early.
keyPoints: commas add extra information about all the students
without commas the clause identifies which students
questions.explanation: Commas can change whether a clause describes everyone or picks out some.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the synonym of 'rapid'.
questions.explanation: 'Rapid' means fast, the same as 'quick'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'generous'.
questions.explanation: A generous person gives freely; a miserly person hates to give.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which word means 'to make a problem or pain less severe'?
questions.explanation: 'Alleviate' means to relieve or reduce; the other words mean to make worse.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which prefix makes the opposite of 'legal'?
questions.explanation: Before the letter l the prefix in- becomes il-: illegal.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the noun form of 'decide'.
questions.explanation: The noun derived from 'decide' is 'decision'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: The word 'meticulous' describes someone who is
questions.explanation: A meticulous person pays close attention to every detail.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Form nouns from the words 'brave', 'wise' and 'free'.
questions.explanation: Suffixes such as -ry, -dom and -om turn adjectives into abstract nouns.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the difference between 'affect' and 'effect', with a sentence for each.
questions.answer: 'Affect' is usually a verb meaning to influence: Rain affects our plans. 'Effect' is usually a noun meaning a result: The effect of the rain was a delay.
keyPoints: affect is usually a verb meaning to influence
effect is usually a noun meaning result
questions.explanation: The two words are often confused because of their similar sound.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'a piece of cake' mean?
questions.explanation: 'A piece of cake' means a task that is very easy.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'to break the ice' mean?
options: to begin a conversation in an awkward situation
questions.explanation: To break the ice is to relieve the tension when people first meet.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does 'once in a blue moon' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means something happens very seldom.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'to bury the hatchet' mean?
options: to end a quarrel and become friends
questions.explanation: To bury the hatchet is to make peace after a disagreement.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the phrasal verb 'give up' mean in 'He gave up smoking'?
questions.explanation: 'Give up' means to stop or abandon a habit or effort.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: The flight was ___ because of fog.
questions.explanation: 'Called off' means cancelled.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Use the idiom 'a blessing in disguise' in a sentence of your own.
questions.answer: Missing the early bus turned out to be a blessing in disguise, because I met my old friend on the next one.
keyPoints: meaning: something that seems bad but proves good
questions.explanation: The idiom describes a misfortune that turns out well.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the meaning of the idiom 'to let the cat out of the bag' and use it in a sentence.
questions.answer: It means to reveal a secret by mistake: Ravi let the cat out of the bag about the surprise party.
keyPoints: means to reveal a secret accidentally
questions.explanation: The idiom is used when a secret is disclosed carelessly.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Meera's grandmother kept a small garden on her terrace. Every morning she watered the tulsi plant first and then the marigolds. She said that plants, like people, need a little care at the same time every day. Meera laughed at first, but after a month of copying her grandmother, she noticed that her own pot of mint had grown twice as tall.' Which plant did the grandmother water first?
questions.explanation: The passage says she watered the tulsi plant first.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Meera's grandmother kept a small garden on her terrace. Every morning she watered the tulsi plant first and then the marigolds. She said that plants, like people, need a little care at the same time every day. Meera laughed at first, but after a month of copying her grandmother, she noticed that her own pot of mint had grown twice as tall.' What did the grandmother mean by care 'at the same time every day'?
options: Plants should be watered only at night
Plants should be watered once a week
Plants do best with a regular routine of care
Plants drink as much as people do
questions.explanation: She compared plants to people and stressed a regular daily routine.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Meera's grandmother kept a small garden on her terrace. Every morning she watered the tulsi plant first and then the marigolds. She said that plants, like people, need a little care at the same time every day. Meera laughed at first, but after a month of copying her grandmother, she noticed that her own pot of mint had grown twice as tall.' What can be inferred about Meera at the end?
options: She was convinced by her grandmother's method after seeing the result
questions.explanation: She copied the routine and saw her mint grow, which suggests she came to believe in it.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Meera's grandmother kept a small garden on her terrace. Every morning she watered the tulsi plant first and then the marigolds. She said that plants, like people, need a little care at the same time every day. Meera laughed at first, but after a month of copying her grandmother, she noticed that her own pot of mint had grown twice as tall.' What changed Meera's attitude towards her grandmother's advice?
questions.answer: After copying her grandmother's routine for a month, Meera saw that her own pot of mint had grown twice as tall.
keyPoints: she followed the routine for a month
her mint plant grew twice as tall
questions.explanation: Seeing the result convinced her.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'The library in our town opens at nine, but Mr. Rao is always there by eight. He sweeps the floor, dusts the shelves and arranges the newspapers on the long table. When asked why he comes so early, he smiles and says, "A reader should find a clean room waiting for him." In twenty years, he has never taken a single day off.' At what time does the library open?
questions.explanation: The passage says it opens at nine.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'The library in our town opens at nine, but Mr. Rao is always there by eight. He sweeps the floor, dusts the shelves and arranges the newspapers on the long table. When asked why he comes so early, he smiles and says, "A reader should find a clean room waiting for him." In twenty years, he has never taken a single day off.' Which of these does the passage NOT say Mr. Rao does before opening?
questions.explanation: Issuing books is not mentioned among his early-morning tasks.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'The library in our town opens at nine, but Mr. Rao is always there by eight. He sweeps the floor, dusts the shelves and arranges the newspapers on the long table. When asked why he comes so early, he smiles and says, "A reader should find a clean room waiting for him." In twenty years, he has never taken a single day off.' Which word best describes Mr. Rao?
questions.explanation: His early arrival and twenty years without a day off show dedication.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'The library in our town opens at nine, but Mr. Rao is always there by eight. He sweeps the floor, dusts the shelves and arranges the newspapers on the long table. When asked why he comes so early, he smiles and says, "A reader should find a clean room waiting for him." In twenty years, he has never taken a single day off.' Why does Mr. Rao reach the library an hour before it opens?
questions.answer: He wants readers to find a clean, tidy room when they arrive.
keyPoints: he cleans and arranges the room
he wants readers to be comfortable
questions.explanation: He gives this reason in his own words.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Last Sunday, a thick fog covered the village. Farmer Karan could not see the road, so he walked slowly with a stick, tapping the ground in front of him. Suddenly, the stick struck something soft. It was a lost calf, shivering near the ditch. Karan wrapped it in his shawl and carried it home.' What did Karan use to find his way?
questions.explanation: He tapped the ground in front of him with a stick.

options: He could not see the road because of the fog
questions.explanation: The thick fog hid the road.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Honey bees communicate by dancing. When a worker bee finds a good source of nectar, she returns to the hive and moves in a pattern called the waggle dance. The direction of the dance shows where the flowers are, and the time she spends waggling tells the other bees how far they must fly.' What is the dance of honey bees called?
questions.explanation: The passage names it the waggle dance.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Honey bees communicate by dancing. When a worker bee finds a good source of nectar, she returns to the hive and moves in a pattern called the waggle dance. The direction of the dance shows where the flowers are, and the time she spends waggling tells the other bees how far they must fly.' What does the direction of the dance tell other bees?
questions.explanation: The passage says the direction shows where the flowers are.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Honey bees communicate by dancing. When a worker bee finds a good source of nectar, she returns to the hive and moves in a pattern called the waggle dance. The direction of the dance shows where the flowers are, and the time she spends waggling tells the other bees how far they must fly.' Which conclusion is supported by the passage?
options: Bees find flowers only by smell
Bees share information with each other about food
Bees dance to scare away enemies
questions.explanation: The dance passes on the location and distance of nectar to other bees.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Honey bees communicate by dancing. When a worker bee finds a good source of nectar, she returns to the hive and moves in a pattern called the waggle dance. The direction of the dance shows where the flowers are, and the time she spends waggling tells the other bees how far they must fly.' How does the waggle dance help the hive?
questions.answer: It tells the other bees where the flowers are and how far to fly, so they can reach the nectar directly.
keyPoints: direction of the dance shows the location of flowers
time spent waggling shows the distance
other bees can fly straight to the nectar

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
questions.explanation: A scientific fact is stated in the simple present; 'water' is singular, so boils.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: We ___ lunch when the guests arrived.
questions.explanation: An action in progress in the past when another action happened needs the past continuous.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: I ___ for the bus for twenty minutes now.
questions.explanation: 'For twenty minutes now' shows an action continuing up to the present: present perfect continuous.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: He said that he ___ the film already.
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb, an earlier completed action takes the past perfect: had seen.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Look! The baby ___.
questions.explanation: 'Look!' points to an action happening now, so the present continuous is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ the match.
questions.explanation: A likely future condition uses the simple present in the if-clause and 'will' in the main clause.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into the past continuous tense: 'They are watching a film.'
questions.explanation: Past continuous is formed with was/were + the -ing form.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Correct the error: 'I am living in this city since 2010.'
questions.answer: I have been living in this city since 2010.
keyPoints: 'since' with a starting point needs a perfect tense
present perfect continuous: have been living
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and continues now with 'since' takes the present perfect (continuous).

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The dog and the cat ___ friends.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: My sister ___ a teacher.
questions.explanation: A singular subject takes 'is'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The news ___ true.
questions.explanation: 'News' looks plural but is an uncountable singular noun.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The scissors ___ on the table.
questions.explanation: 'Scissors' is a plural noun and takes a plural verb.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Rohit, along with his friends, ___ going to the fair.
questions.explanation: 'Along with' does not make the subject plural; the verb agrees with 'Rohit'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: The books is on the table.
Each of the players has a bottle.
questions.explanation: 'Each of' takes a singular verb: has.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Correct the error: 'The boys in the team was happy.'
questions.answer: The boys in the team were happy.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the subject 'boys', not with 'team'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Complete with 'is' or 'are' and give the reason: 'A pair of gloves ___ on the table.'
questions.answer: is. The subject is 'pair', which is singular, even though 'gloves' is plural.
keyPoints: pair is singular so the verb is 'is'
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the head noun, not the noun in the phrase after 'of'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct article: He is ___ engineer.
questions.explanation: 'Engineer' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct article: We saw ___ one-eyed man.
questions.explanation: 'One' starts with a 'w' sound, a consonant sound, so 'a' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct article: ___ Himalayas are the highest mountains in the world.
questions.explanation: Mountain ranges take the definite article: the Himalayas.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ of the two shirts fits me.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is used for two things; 'none' is used for three or more.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: There are ___ mangoes in the basket.
questions.explanation: 'Mangoes' is countable and plural, so 'many' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: The teacher gave us some useful advice.
questions.explanation: 'Advice', 'information' and 'furniture' are uncountable and have no plural form or 'a'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Fill in with 'much' or 'many': (a) How ___ water is left? (b) How ___ books do you have?
keyPoints: much with uncountable nouns like water
many with countable plural nouns like books
questions.explanation: Choose the determiner according to whether the noun is countable.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Why is 'the' used before 'sun' in 'The sun is a star'?
questions.answer: Because there is only one sun that everybody knows about, so the definite article is used with it.
keyPoints: unique things take the definite article
questions.explanation: The is used with things that are the only one of their kind.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: She was born ___ 2008.
questions.explanation: 'In' is used with years.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: The book is ___ the table.
questions.explanation: 'On' shows that something rests on a surface.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: He apologised ___ being late.
questions.explanation: The verb 'apologise' is followed by 'for'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: We walked ___ the bridge to reach the other bank.
questions.explanation: 'Across' shows movement from one side to the other.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: I will wait here ___ you come back.
questions.explanation: 'Until' shows the time up to which the waiting continues.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: The adjective 'good' takes 'at' when talking about a skill.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Fill in the blanks with prepositions: 'He is fond ___ music and is married ___ a doctor.'
questions.explanation: These adjectives take fixed prepositions.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Rewrite using 'unless': 'If you do not hurry, you will miss the train.'
questions.answer: Unless you hurry, you will miss the train.
keyPoints: verb in the unless-clause is not negative
questions.explanation: 'Unless' already carries the negative meaning.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: Birds ___ fly, but fish cannot.
questions.explanation: 'Can' expresses ability.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ you help me with this bag?
questions.explanation: 'Can you...?' is a common way to ask for help.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: Look at those dark clouds. It ___ rain soon.
questions.explanation: 'May' expresses a possibility based on what we see.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ like a cup of tea, please.
questions.explanation: 'Would like' is the polite way of saying what one wants.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: You ___ see a doctor; your fever is high.
questions.explanation: 'Should' is used to give advice.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: A modal verb is followed by the base form of the verb, without 'to' or -s.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Rewrite using 'must': 'It is necessary for every student to wear a uniform.'
questions.answer: Every student must wear a uniform.
keyPoints: base form of the verb follows
questions.explanation: 'Must' states an obligation briefly.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the difference between 'You needn't go' and 'You mustn't go'.
questions.answer: 'You needn't go' means it is not necessary for you to go. 'You mustn't go' means you are forbidden to go.
questions.explanation: Needn't removes an obligation, while mustn't forbids an action.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The window ___ by Rahul.
questions.explanation: The passive of the simple past is was + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The cake ___ by my mother.
questions.explanation: The subject receives the action, so the passive 'was baked' is needed.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'She has finished the work.'
options: The work is finished by her.
The work has been finished by her.
The work was finished by her.
The work had been finished by her.
questions.explanation: Present perfect active becomes has/have been + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'Open the door.'
questions.explanation: An imperative becomes passive with 'Let ... be + past participle'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'People speak Hindi here.'
questions.explanation: Simple present passive: is/are + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: The mural was painted by the artist.
questions.explanation: In the passive the subject (mural) receives the action.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into the passive voice: 'The students are planting trees.'
questions.answer: Trees are being planted by the students.
questions.explanation: Present continuous passive is am/is/are being + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into the active voice: 'By whom was the window broken?'
questions.explanation: The doer of the action becomes the subject of the active question.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I like mangoes.'
options: He said that he liked mangoes.
He said that I liked mangoes.
He said that he would like mangoes.
He said that he liking mangoes.
questions.explanation: Present tense becomes past tense and 'I' becomes 'he'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said, 'I am reading a novel.'
options: She said that she has been reading a novel.
She said that I was reading a novel.
She said that she was reading a novel.
She said that she is read a novel.
questions.explanation: Present continuous changes to past continuous and the pronoun to 'she'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: The boy said, 'I have finished my work.'
options: The boy said that I had finished my work.
The boy said that he would finish his work.
The boy said that he has finished my work.
The boy said that he had finished his work.
questions.explanation: Present perfect becomes past perfect, and 'I' and 'my' become 'he' and 'his'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He asked, 'What is your name?'
options: He asked me what is my name.
He asked me what my name was.
He asked me what was your name.
He asked me that what my name was.
questions.explanation: The question becomes a statement in order, the tense changes, and 'your' becomes 'my'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: The teacher said to the boys, 'Be quiet.'
options: The teacher said the boys that be quiet.
The teacher told the boys they are quiet.
The teacher ordered the boys to be quiet.
The teacher asked the boys if they were quiet.
questions.explanation: A command is reported with 'ordered/told ... to + verb'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said to me, 'Where did you go yesterday?'
options: He asked me where I had gone the day before.
He asked me where did I go yesterday.
He asked me where you had gone the day before.
He asked me where I have gone the day before.
questions.explanation: Past simple becomes past perfect, 'you' becomes 'I', and 'yesterday' becomes 'the day before'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into indirect speech: Priya said, 'I bought a new bag yesterday.'
questions.answer: Priya said that she had bought a new bag the day before.
questions.explanation: Apply the usual changes of tense, pronoun and time word.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into direct speech: The captain told the players to practise daily.
questions.answer: The captain said to the players, 'Practise daily.'
questions.explanation: A reported command becomes an imperative sentence in direct speech.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: A group of words that has its own subject and verb is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A clause contains a subject and a predicate, unlike a phrase.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which of these is a simple sentence?
options: I stayed home because I was ill.
The man who called is my uncle.
The children played in the park.
questions.explanation: A simple sentence has one subject and one finite verb.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Combine using 'not only ... but also': 'He is intelligent. He is hardworking.'
options: He is not only intelligent and also hardworking.
He is intelligent not only but also hardworking.
Not only he is intelligent but also hardworking.
He is not only intelligent but also hardworking.
questions.explanation: The two parts of the pair must be placed directly before the words they join.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into an exclamatory sentence: 'It is a very beautiful garden.'
options: How a beautiful garden it is!
What a beautiful garden it is!
What beautiful a garden it is!
questions.explanation: 'What a + adjective + noun' forms an exclamation.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence means the same as 'Gold is more precious than silver'?
options: Silver is as precious as gold.
Gold is as precious as silver.
Silver is not so precious as gold.
Silver is more precious than gold.
questions.explanation: If gold is more precious, then silver is less precious: not so precious as gold.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence contains an adjective clause?
options: The book that I borrowed is interesting.
He ran so that he could catch the bus.
I think that she is right.
When it rains, I stay in.
questions.explanation: 'That I borrowed' describes the noun 'book'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Rewrite as a negative sentence without changing the meaning: 'He always speaks the truth.'
questions.explanation: A positive statement can be turned into a negative one with the opposite word.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Rewrite using 'too ... to': 'He is so tired that he cannot walk.'
questions.answer: He is too tired to walk.
questions.explanation: 'Too ... to' already has a negative sense.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which punctuation mark is used at the end of a statement?
questions.explanation: A full stop ends a statement.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which words need capital letters in: 'we visited delhi last june.'?
questions.explanation: The first word of a sentence, names of places and names of months begin with capitals.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly for several boys?
options: The boys' hostel is near the gate.
The boy's' hostel is near the gate.
The boys's hostel is near the gate.
The boys hostel's is near the gate.
questions.explanation: For a plural noun ending in -s, the apostrophe goes after the s.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
options: She bought: milk, eggs and bread.
He said: that he was late.
You will need these items: a pen, a ruler and a notebook.
questions.explanation: A colon follows a complete statement to introduce a list.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: Well, I think you are right.
Well I think, you are right.
Well I think you are right,
Well. I think, you are right.
questions.explanation: A comma follows the introductory word 'Well'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: 'I am late', said Anil 'because the bus broke down'.
'I am late' said Anil, 'because the bus broke down.'
'I am late,' said Anil, 'because the bus broke down.'
'I am late,' said Anil. 'because the bus broke down.'
questions.explanation: A comma goes inside the first quotation and another after the speaker tag, because the sentence continues.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Punctuate correctly: where are you going asked the guard
questions.answer: 'Where are you going?' asked the guard.
keyPoints: question mark inside the inverted commas
questions.explanation: A question in direct speech keeps its question mark before the closing quote.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the difference between 'its' and 'it's'.
questions.answer: 'Its' is a possessive word meaning belonging to it. 'It's' is the short form of 'it is' or 'it has'.
keyPoints: it's is a contraction of it is / it has
questions.explanation: The apostrophe in it's marks missing letters, not possession.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the synonym of 'enormous'.
questions.explanation: 'Enormous' means very large, like 'huge'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'ancient'.
questions.explanation: 'Ancient' means very old; its opposite is 'modern'.

questions.q: A person who writes poems is called a
questions.explanation: A poet writes poetry.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Necessary' has one c and two s's.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: The suffix -less in 'careless' means
questions.explanation: -less means without: careless means without care.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which pair of words are homophones?
questions.explanation: Homophones sound the same but differ in meaning and spelling; flour and flower are pronounced alike.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Write the antonyms of 'victory', 'success' and 'hope'.
questions.explanation: Antonyms are words of opposite meaning.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Form adjectives from the words 'beauty', 'courage' and 'harm'.
questions.explanation: Suffixes such as -ful and -ous turn nouns into adjectives.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'under the weather' mean?
questions.explanation: To be under the weather is to feel unwell.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'to spill the beans' mean?
questions.explanation: To spill the beans is to give away a secret.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'to cost an arm and a leg' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means to be extremely expensive.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'to hit the nail on the head' mean?
options: to say or do exactly the right thing
questions.explanation: It means to be exactly right about something.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the phrasal verb 'look after' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Look after' means to take care of someone or something.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: The teacher asked us to ___ the lesson before the test.
questions.explanation: 'Go over' means to review or check carefully.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the idiom 'to turn over a new leaf' and use it in a sentence.
questions.answer: It means to start behaving in a better way: After failing the test, Sam turned over a new leaf and began to study daily.
keyPoints: means to make a fresh, better start
questions.explanation: The idiom is about changing one's habits for the better.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the phrasal verb 'put off' and use it in a sentence.
questions.answer: 'Put off' means to postpone: The school put off the picnic because of rain.
questions.explanation: 'Put off' is used when an event is moved to a later time.

questions.subject: english

questions.subject: english

questions.explanation: He found his mother in the third row.

options: He took a deep breath and looked at one friendly face

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Next week at this time, we ___ on a beach in Goa.
questions.explanation: An action in progress at a future time uses the future continuous.

questions.explanation: A finished time expression requires the simple past.
