questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: The trousers is in the cupboard.
A bunch of keys was found on the road.
questions.explanation: The subject 'bunch' is singular, so the verb is 'was'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Correct the error: 'The list of items are on the desk.'
questions.answer: The list of items is on the desk.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with 'list', not with 'items'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Complete and explain: 'Two-thirds of the apples ___ rotten.'
questions.answer: are. A fraction takes its verb from the noun after 'of', and 'apples' is plural.
keyPoints: verb agrees with the noun after 'of'
questions.explanation: With fractions, the noun that follows decides the verb.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct article: My mother bought ___ umbrella.
questions.explanation: 'Umbrella' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct article: She has ___ unique collection of stamps.
questions.explanation: 'Unique' begins with a 'yoo' sound, a consonant sound, so 'a' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct article: ___ Indian Ocean lies to the south of India.
questions.explanation: Names of oceans take the definite article.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: I have ___ friends in this city, so I feel at home.
questions.explanation: 'Friends' is countable and plural, so 'many' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: There is very ___ sugar in my tea; it tastes bitter.
questions.explanation: 'Sugar' is uncountable, and 'very little' means hardly any.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: The honesty is the best policy.
I need an hour to finish the work.
questions.explanation: 'Hour' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is correct; the other sentences misuse articles.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Fill in with a, an or the: 'He is ___ best player in ___ team.'
questions.explanation: Superlatives take 'the'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain why 'the' is used in 'The poor need our help.'
questions.answer: 'The' before an adjective such as 'poor' makes it refer to a whole class of people, here all poor people, and the phrase takes a plural verb.
keyPoints: the + adjective names a class of people
questions.explanation: This construction turns an adjective into a group noun.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: The teacher divided the sweets ___ the twenty children.
questions.explanation: 'Among' is used for more than two persons or things.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: She came to school ___ foot.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'on foot'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: Mr. Das has been teaching here ___ twenty years.
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a period of time.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: I prefer tea ___ coffee.
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' is followed by 'to', not 'than'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: He worked hard ___ he could pass the examination.
questions.explanation: 'So that' introduces a purpose.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: The verb 'insist' takes the preposition 'on'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Combine using 'because': 'He was absent. He was ill.'
questions.answer: He was absent because he was ill.
questions.explanation: 'Because' joins an effect with its cause.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Fill in the blanks with prepositions: 'She was angry ___ me ___ forgetting her book.'
questions.explanation: We are angry with a person and for something done.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ ride a bicycle when I was six.
questions.explanation: 'Could' expresses ability in the past.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ I come in, sir?
questions.explanation: 'May I' is used to ask for permission.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: He ___ be at home; his car is outside.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses a logical conclusion from evidence.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ you like some more rice?
questions.explanation: 'Would you like...?' is the polite way to make an offer.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: Students ___ keep silence in the library.
questions.explanation: 'Should' expresses duty or what is expected.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence shows a prohibition?
options: You must not enter this room.
You need not enter this room.
questions.explanation: 'Must not' forbids an action.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Rewrite using 'can': 'She is able to solve the problem.'
keyPoints: base form of the verb follows
questions.explanation: 'Is able to' and 'can' both express ability.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain why 'He can swims' is wrong and write the correct sentence.
questions.answer: A modal verb is followed by the base form of the verb, with no -s. The correct sentence is 'He can swim.'
questions.explanation: Modal verbs do not change form for the third person.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The song ___ by the children.
questions.explanation: The passive of the simple past is was + past participle (sung).

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Letters ___ by the postman every day.
questions.explanation: A plural subject in the simple present passive takes 'are + past participle'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'He had written a letter.'
options: A letter was written by him.
A letter had been written by him.
A letter has been written by him.
A letter is written by him.
questions.explanation: Past perfect active becomes had been + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'Do you know him?'
options: Does he be known to you?
questions.explanation: Simple present questions become 'Is/Are + subject + past participle', and 'know' usually takes 'to'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'She will sing a song.'
options: A song will be sung by her.
A song will sung by her.
A song would be sung by her.
A song is sung by her.
questions.explanation: Future passive: will be + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is in the active voice?
options: The farmers grow rice in Punjab.
questions.explanation: In 'The farmers grow rice' the subject performs the action.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into the passive voice: 'The gardener waters the plants every morning.'
questions.answer: The plants are watered by the gardener every morning.
questions.explanation: Simple present passive is is/are + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into the passive voice: 'People say that honesty is the best policy.'
questions.answer: It is said that honesty is the best policy.
questions.explanation: Sentences with 'say that' often take the passive form 'It is said that'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said, 'I live in Pune.'
options: She said that she lived in Pune.
She said that I lived in Pune.
She said that she would live in Pune.
She said that she had live in Pune.
questions.explanation: The present tense becomes the past, and 'I' becomes 'she'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I can swim.'
options: He said that I could swim.
He said that he would swim.
He said that he could swim.
He said that he can to swim.
questions.explanation: 'Can' changes to 'could' and 'I' to 'he'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said, 'My brother is coming today.'
options: She said that my brother was coming that day.
She said that her brother had come that day.
She said that her brother would come the next day.
She said that her brother was coming that day.
questions.explanation: 'My' becomes 'her', 'is coming' becomes 'was coming', and 'today' becomes 'that day'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said to her, 'Are you ready?'
options: He asked her that she was ready.
He asked her if she was ready.
He asked her was she ready.
He asked her what she was ready.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with 'if', in statement order.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: The mother said to the child, 'Please sit down.'
options: The mother said to the child that please sit down.
The mother requested the child that sit down.
The mother requested the child to sit down.
The mother asked the child sit down.
questions.explanation: A polite request is reported with 'requested ... to + verb'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: Rahul said, 'Hurrah! We have won the match.'
options: Rahul exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
Rahul exclaimed with joy that we had won the match.
Rahul exclaimed with sorrow that they had won the match.
Rahul exclaimed with joy that they would win the match.
questions.explanation: 'Hurrah' shows joy; 'we' becomes 'they' and the present perfect becomes the past perfect.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into indirect speech: Seema said to me, 'I will help you.'
questions.answer: Seema told me that she would help me.
keyPoints: pronouns change: I to she, you to me
questions.explanation: Reporting changes the tense and the pronouns.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into direct speech: She asked him whether he had seen her bag.
questions.answer: She said to him, 'Have you seen my bag?'
keyPoints: question order restored with a question mark
he becomes you, her becomes my, had seen becomes have seen
questions.explanation: A reported yes/no question becomes a direct question with inverted word order.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which of these is a coordinating conjunction?
questions.explanation: 'But' joins two clauses of equal rank; the others introduce subordinate clauses.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which of these is a complex sentence?
options: I did not go because it was raining.
questions.explanation: It has a main clause and a subordinate clause beginning with 'because'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Combine using a relative pronoun: 'The man is my uncle. He lives next door.'
options: The man who is my uncle who lives next door.
The man which lives next door is my uncle.
The man whom lives next door is my uncle.
The man who lives next door is my uncle.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the subject of 'lives' and refers to a person.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change the degree: 'Iron is the most useful metal.'
options: Iron is as useful as any other metal.
Iron is more useful than any other metal.
Iron is the more useful than other metal.
Iron is useful than any metal.
questions.explanation: The superlative is rewritten as a comparative with 'than any other'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Rewrite in the negative form: 'Everyone likes ice cream.'
questions.explanation: 'Nobody dislikes' keeps the original meaning in a negative form.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence contains a noun clause?
options: I do not know where she lives.
The girl who lives here is kind.
Because he was late, he was scolded.
questions.explanation: 'Where she lives' is the object of 'know' and so acts as a noun.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into an assertive sentence: 'Who can doubt his honesty?'
questions.answer: No one can doubt his honesty.
questions.explanation: A rhetorical 'Who can...?' means 'No one can...'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Combine using a participle: 'She finished her work. She went out to play.'
questions.answer: Having finished her work, she went out to play.
questions.explanation: A participle phrase shows that one action was completed before the other.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: A direct question ends with a question mark and begins with a capital letter.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence has correct capital letters?
questions.explanation: The first word of a sentence and the name of a city begin with capitals.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
options: Delhi, the capital of India, is a big city.
Delhi the capital, of India is a big city.
Delhi, the capital of India is, a big city.
Delhi the capital of India, is a big city.
questions.explanation: Commas enclose a phrase that adds extra information.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct possessive form: The ___ playground is closed.
questions.explanation: 'Children' is an irregular plural not ending in s, so 's is added.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence uses hyphens correctly?
questions.explanation: The compound noun is written sister-in-law with two hyphens.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: The exclamation mark goes inside the quotation marks, and the speaker tag begins with a small letter.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Punctuate correctly: the boy asked his mother may i go out to play
questions.answer: The boy asked his mother, 'May I go out to play?'
keyPoints: capital letters for The and May
inverted commas and a question mark
questions.explanation: The spoken question is placed in inverted commas and ends with a question mark.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Insert the missing commas: My teacher Mr Rao who is very strict gave us extra homework.
questions.answer: My teacher, Mr Rao, who is very strict, gave us extra homework.
keyPoints: commas around the name Mr Rao
commas around the clause who is very strict
questions.explanation: Commas set off extra information that can be removed without changing the main sentence.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the synonym of 'begin'.
questions.explanation: 'Begin' and 'start' have the same meaning.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'brave'.
questions.explanation: A brave person is fearless; a cowardly person is full of fear.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What is a person who travels on foot called?
questions.explanation: A pedestrian walks along roads rather than travelling in a vehicle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Separate' has an 'a' after the p: sep-a-rate.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: The prefix 'mis-' in 'misunderstand' means
questions.explanation: 'Mis-' means wrongly or badly.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: If a person is 'reluctant' to speak, he is
questions.explanation: 'Reluctant' means unwilling or hesitant.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Write the plural forms of 'child', 'tooth' and 'sheep'.
questions.explanation: These are irregular plurals.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the difference between 'principal' and 'principle', with a sentence for each.
questions.answer: 'Principal' means the head of a school (or main): The principal addressed us. 'Principle' means a rule or belief: Honesty is a good principle.
keyPoints: principal = head of a school or chief
questions.explanation: The words sound alike but differ in meaning.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'break a leg' mean when said before a performance?
questions.explanation: It is a way of wishing a performer good luck.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'it is raining cats and dogs' mean?
options: Animals are falling from the sky.
questions.explanation: The idiom means heavy rain.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'to call it a day' mean?
options: to stop working for the day
questions.explanation: It means to stop doing something, usually work, for the time being.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does 'the black sheep of the family' mean?
options: a person who is seen as a disgrace to the family
questions.explanation: The black sheep is a member who is regarded as a failure or disgrace.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the phrasal verb 'carry out' mean in 'The doctors carried out the test'?
questions.explanation: 'Carry out' means to do or perform a task.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: The hikers had to ___ the climb because of the storm.
questions.explanation: 'Give up' means to abandon an effort.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the idiom 'to add fuel to the fire' and use it in a sentence.
questions.answer: It means to make a bad situation worse: His angry reply only added fuel to the fire.
keyPoints: means to worsen a difficult situation
questions.explanation: The idiom compares making things worse to feeding a fire.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the phrasal verb 'run out of' and use it in a sentence.
questions.answer: 'Run out of' means to have no more of something: We ran out of milk this morning.
questions.explanation: It is used when a supply is finished.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Ladakh is a cold desert high in the mountains. It receives very little rain, and winter temperatures can fall far below freezing. Even so, farmers there grow barley and apricots, using water from melting glaciers carried through narrow channels to their fields.' What do farmers in Ladakh grow, according to the passage?
questions.explanation: The last sentence names barley and apricots.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Ladakh is a cold desert high in the mountains. It receives very little rain, and winter temperatures can fall far below freezing. Even so, farmers there grow barley and apricots, using water from melting glaciers carried through narrow channels to their fields.' Where do the farmers get water for their fields?
questions.explanation: They use glacier water carried through channels.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Ladakh is a cold desert high in the mountains. It receives very little rain, and winter temperatures can fall far below freezing. Even so, farmers there grow barley and apricots, using water from melting glaciers carried through narrow channels to their fields.' Why is Ladakh described as a 'cold desert'?
options: It is cold and receives very little rain
It is full of sand dunes
questions.explanation: A desert gets very little rain; Ladakh also has freezing winters.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Ladakh is a cold desert high in the mountains. It receives very little rain, and winter temperatures can fall far below freezing. Even so, farmers there grow barley and apricots, using water from melting glaciers carried through narrow channels to their fields.' How do Ladakh's farmers manage to grow crops despite the harsh climate?
questions.answer: They bring water from melting glaciers through narrow channels to their fields and grow crops such as barley and apricots.
keyPoints: grow hardy crops like barley and apricots
questions.explanation: Channelling glacier meltwater makes up for the lack of rain.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'The old clock in the village square had stopped years ago, but nobody had bothered to repair it. One day, a young boy named Imran climbed the tower with a small toolbox. After two days of patient work, the hands began to move again. People gathered below and cheered, and the first chime rang out across the fields.' Who repaired the clock?
questions.explanation: The boy named Imran did the repair.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'The old clock in the village square had stopped years ago, but nobody had bothered to repair it. One day, a young boy named Imran climbed the tower with a small toolbox. After two days of patient work, the hands began to move again. People gathered below and cheered, and the first chime rang out across the fields.' How long did Imran take to repair the clock?
questions.explanation: The passage says he worked for two days.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'The old clock in the village square had stopped years ago, but nobody had bothered to repair it. One day, a young boy named Imran climbed the tower with a small toolbox. After two days of patient work, the hands began to move again. People gathered below and cheered, and the first chime rang out across the fields.' What does 'patient work' tell us about Imran?
options: He worked carefully without giving up
questions.explanation: Patient work over two days shows steady effort.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'The old clock in the village square had stopped years ago, but nobody had bothered to repair it. One day, a young boy named Imran climbed the tower with a small toolbox. After two days of patient work, the hands began to move again. People gathered below and cheered, and the first chime rang out across the fields.' How did the villagers react when the clock started again?
questions.answer: They gathered below the tower and cheered.
questions.explanation: The passage states their reaction directly.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'The Great Indian bustard is a large bird found in dry grasslands. Its numbers have fallen sharply because its grassland habitat has been turned into farms, and because power lines in its path are dangerous. Conservation groups are protecting nesting areas and marking power lines so that birds can see them.' Where is the Great Indian bustard found?
questions.explanation: The first sentence says dry grasslands.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'The Great Indian bustard is a large bird found in dry grasslands. Its numbers have fallen sharply because its grassland habitat has been turned into farms, and because power lines in its path are dangerous. Conservation groups are protecting nesting areas and marking power lines so that birds can see them.' Which threat to the bird is mentioned?
questions.explanation: Its habitat has been turned into farms.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'The Great Indian bustard is a large bird found in dry grasslands. Its numbers have fallen sharply because its grassland habitat has been turned into farms, and because power lines in its path are dangerous. Conservation groups are protecting nesting areas and marking power lines so that birds can see them.' Why are power lines being marked?
options: So that birds can see them and avoid them
questions.explanation: The passage states the purpose: birds can see them.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'The Great Indian bustard is a large bird found in dry grasslands. Its numbers have fallen sharply because its grassland habitat has been turned into farms, and because power lines in its path are dangerous. Conservation groups are protecting nesting areas and marking power lines so that birds can see them.' Name two causes of the fall in numbers and one step taken to help the bird.
questions.answer: Causes: grassland turned into farms and dangerous power lines. Step: protecting nesting areas (or marking power lines).
keyPoints: protecting nesting areas or marking power lines
questions.explanation: The passage lists both causes and the conservation steps.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Kavya's school bus broke down halfway to the museum. While the driver called for help, the teacher suggested a game: each student had to describe the museum they imagined. By the time a new bus arrived, the children had spoken about robots, dinosaurs and ancient coins, and nobody was grumbling about the delay.' What happened to the school bus?
questions.explanation: The bus broke down halfway.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Kavya's school bus broke down halfway to the museum. While the driver called for help, the teacher suggested a game: each student had to describe the museum they imagined. By the time a new bus arrived, the children had spoken about robots, dinosaurs and ancient coins, and nobody was grumbling about the delay.' What did the teacher suggest?
options: A game of describing an imagined museum
questions.explanation: The teacher proposed that each student describe the museum they imagined.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Kavya's school bus broke down halfway to the museum. While the driver called for help, the teacher suggested a game: each student had to describe the museum they imagined. By the time a new bus arrived, the children had spoken about robots, dinosaurs and ancient coins, and nobody was grumbling about the delay.' What does the passage suggest about the teacher's idea?
options: It kept the children cheerful during the wait
questions.explanation: Nobody grumbled about the delay, so the game worked.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Kavya's school bus broke down halfway to the museum. While the driver called for help, the teacher suggested a game: each student had to describe the museum they imagined. By the time a new bus arrived, the children had spoken about robots, dinosaurs and ancient coins, and nobody was grumbling about the delay.' How did the children spend the time while waiting?
questions.answer: They played a game in which each described an imagined museum, talking about robots, dinosaurs and ancient coins.
questions.explanation: The passage describes the game and what the children said.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: My grandmother ___ tea every morning.
questions.explanation: A habit with a singular subject takes the simple present with -s.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Listen! Someone ___ at the door.
questions.explanation: 'Listen!' points to an action happening now, so the present continuous is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: I ___ him since childhood.
questions.explanation: 'Since childhood' with a state continuing to now needs the present perfect: have known.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The match ___ before we reached the ground.
questions.explanation: The match started before another past action, so the past perfect is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: This time tomorrow, I ___ an exam.
questions.explanation: An action in progress at a particular future time takes the future continuous.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: When I will reach, I will call you.
If he will come, I will go.
When I reach home, I will call you.
I will call you when I will reach.
questions.explanation: After 'when' and 'if' referring to the future, the simple present is used, not 'will'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into the present perfect tense: 'They finished the project.'
questions.explanation: The present perfect uses have/has with the past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Correct the error: 'Since morning it is raining.'
questions.answer: It has been raining since morning.
keyPoints: present perfect continuous: has been raining
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and still continues takes the present perfect continuous.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The flowers ___ beautiful.
questions.explanation: 'Flowers' is plural, so the verb is 'are'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: He ___ his homework daily.
questions.explanation: A singular subject takes 'does' in the simple present.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Everyone ___ invited to the party.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' is singular, so it takes 'is'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The principal and the teachers ___ present.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by 'and' are plural.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The quality of these mangoes ___ excellent.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'quality', which is singular.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: The cattle is grazing in the field.
The news were broadcast at nine.
Neither the boy nor the girl was absent.
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'girl', which is singular.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Correct the error: 'The sceneries of Kashmir is charming.'
questions.answer: The scenery of Kashmir is charming.
keyPoints: scenery is uncountable and has no plural
questions.explanation: 'Scenery' is an uncountable noun.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Complete and explain: 'The Arabian Nights ___ a collection of stories.'
questions.answer: is. The title names a single work, so it takes a singular verb even though it looks plural.
keyPoints: title of one book is singular
questions.explanation: The title of a single book or film takes a singular verb.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct article: I read ___ interesting article.
questions.explanation: 'Interesting' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct article: He bought ___ useful book.
questions.explanation: 'Useful' begins with a 'yoo' consonant sound, so 'a' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct article: ___ Taj Mahal is in Agra.
questions.explanation: A well-known unique building takes the definite article.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: He has ___ interest in sports, so he rarely plays.
questions.explanation: 'Interest' is uncountable, and 'little' means hardly any.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ student must carry an identity card.
questions.explanation: 'Every' is followed by a singular noun.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: The Mount Everest is the highest peak.
She is an one-rupee coin collector.
My brother wants to be an astronaut.
questions.explanation: 'Astronaut' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is correct.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Fill in with 'some' or 'any': (a) I have ___ questions. (b) Do you have ___ questions?
questions.explanation: 'Some' is normally used in affirmative sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the difference in meaning between 'a few' and 'few'.
questions.answer: 'A few' means some, a small number (a positive idea). 'Few' means hardly any (a negative idea).
questions.explanation: The article changes the meaning from positive to negative.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: The picture is hanging ___ the wall.
questions.explanation: 'On' is used for something attached to a surface.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: He jumped ___ the river.
questions.explanation: 'Into' shows movement to the inside of something.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: She is interested ___ painting.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'interested' is followed by 'in'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: He has been absent ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: She is poor, ___ she is happy.
questions.explanation: 'But' links two contrasting ideas.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Adjectives such as senior and junior are followed by 'to', not 'than'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Join using 'so that': 'She saved money. She could buy a bicycle.'
questions.answer: She saved money so that she could buy a bicycle.
questions.explanation: 'So that' joins a purpose clause to the main clause.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Fill in the blanks with prepositions: 'The children were excited ___ the trip, and they thanked their teacher ___ organising it.'
questions.explanation: These words take fixed prepositions.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: Cats ___ see in dim light.
questions.explanation: 'Can' expresses ability.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ I help you with your bag?
questions.explanation: 'Shall I...?' is used to offer help.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: She has worked for sixteen hours, so she ___ be very tired.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses a strong logical conclusion.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: You ___ better take a taxi; it is getting late.
questions.explanation: 'Had better' is a fixed expression for strong advice.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ rather walk than take a bus.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' expresses preference.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence expresses ability?
questions.explanation: 'Can speak' says that she is able to speak four languages.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Rewrite using 'may': 'Perhaps it will rain tomorrow.'
questions.explanation: 'May' replaces 'perhaps ... will'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the difference between 'He used to play cricket' and 'He is used to playing cricket'.
questions.answer: 'Used to play' describes a habit in the past that no longer exists. 'Is used to playing' means he is accustomed to playing now.
questions.explanation: The two structures look alike but have different meanings.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The thief ___ by the police.
questions.explanation: The thief receives the action, so the passive 'was caught' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: A new school ___ in our town.
questions.explanation: The school receives the action in progress: is being built.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'Mohan is writing a letter.'
options: A letter is written by Mohan.
A letter is being written by Mohan.
A letter was being written by Mohan.
A letter has been written by Mohan.
questions.explanation: Present continuous active becomes is/are being + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'They have sold the house.'
options: The house is sold by them.
The house was sold by them.
The house had been sold by them.
The house has been sold by them.
questions.explanation: Present perfect active becomes has/have been + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'Who broke the vase?'
options: By whom was the vase broken?
By whom the vase was broken?
Who is the vase broken by?
questions.explanation: 'Who' becomes 'By whom' and the verb moves to was + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which of these sentences cannot be changed into the passive voice?
questions.explanation: 'Shines' is intransitive, so there is no object to become the subject.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into the passive voice: 'The principal gave the prizes.'
questions.answer: The prizes were given by the principal.
questions.explanation: Simple past passive: was/were + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into the passive voice: 'Someone has stolen my bicycle.'
questions.explanation: The vague agent 'someone' is normally left out in the passive.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: Ravi said, 'We are late.'
options: Ravi said that they were late.
Ravi said that we were late.
Ravi said that they had been late.
Ravi said that he was late.
questions.explanation: 'We' becomes 'they' and 'are' becomes 'were'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said, 'I have lost my pen.'
options: She said that she lost my pen.
She said that I had lost my pen.
She said that she had lost her pen.
She said that she would lose her pen.
questions.explanation: Present perfect becomes past perfect; 'I' and 'my' become 'she' and 'her'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I will come tomorrow.'
options: He said that he will come the next day.
He said that I would come the next day.
He said that he came the next day.
He said that he would come the next day.
questions.explanation: 'Will' becomes 'would' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She asked me, 'Why are you crying?'
options: She asked me why was I crying.
She asked me why I was crying.
She asked me why you were crying.
She asked me that why I was crying.
questions.explanation: The wh-question keeps its question word but takes statement order.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: The officer said to the driver, 'Do not park here.'
options: The officer told the driver do not park here.
The officer said to the driver not park there.
The officer told the driver not to park there.
The officer told the driver that do not park there.
questions.explanation: A negative command is reported with 'told ... not to + verb', and 'here' becomes 'there'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: Anu said, 'What a lovely garden!'
options: Anu exclaimed with delight that it was a lovely garden.
Anu said what a lovely garden!
Anu asked what a lovely garden it was.
Anu exclaimed that she had a lovely garden.
questions.explanation: An exclamation is reported as a statement with 'exclaimed with delight that'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into indirect speech: The boy said to his father, 'I need a new bag.'
questions.answer: The boy told his father that he needed a new bag.
questions.explanation: The present tense moves back to the past tense.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into direct speech: The teacher asked Mohan why he had not done his homework.
questions.answer: The teacher said to Mohan, 'Why have you not done your homework?'
keyPoints: he becomes you, his becomes your, had not done becomes have not done
questions.explanation: A reported wh-question becomes a direct question again.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: A sentence that gives an order or a request is called
questions.explanation: An imperative sentence gives a command or request.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What kind of sentence is this? 'He is rich, yet he is unhappy.'
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined by 'yet', a coordinating conjunction.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Combine using 'although': 'She is old. She works hard.'
options: Although she is old and works hard.
She works hard although old she is.
She is old although she works hard.
Although she is old, she works hard.
questions.explanation: 'Although' introduces the concession, followed by the main clause.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into an interrogative sentence: 'He is a doctor.'
questions.explanation: The verb 'is' is moved before the subject to form a question.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence means the same as 'Sita is wiser than Gita'?
options: Gita is as wise as Sita.
Sita is not as wise as Gita.
Gita is not so wise as Sita.
questions.explanation: If Sita is wiser, then Gita is not so wise as Sita.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence contains an adverb clause of reason?
options: She was happy because she had passed.
She said that she had passed.
The girl who passed is happy.
questions.explanation: 'Because she had passed' gives the reason for her happiness.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into a complex sentence: 'Hearing the news, she wept.'
questions.answer: When she heard the news, she wept.
keyPoints: participle phrase becomes a subordinate clause
questions.explanation: A participle phrase can be expanded into an adverb clause of time.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Combine using 'neither ... nor': 'He did not call. He did not write.'
keyPoints: neither ... nor joins the two verbs
questions.explanation: 'Neither ... nor' already contains the negation.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: 'It's' is the contraction of 'it is' and needs an apostrophe.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
options: Diwali is a festival of lights.
questions.explanation: The first word of a sentence and the name of a festival begin with capitals.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence uses the comma correctly?
options: After the match, the players went home.
After the match the players, went home.
After, the match the players went home.
After the match the players went, home.
questions.explanation: A comma follows an introductory phrase.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: A comma introduces the quotation, and the full stop goes inside the closing quotation mark.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence has the apostrophe in the correct place?
questions.explanation: The apostrophe takes the place of the missing letter o in 'do not'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: My favourite fruits are: mangoes, grapes and apples.
I bought a bag; a pen; and a book.
He was late; therefore, he missed the bus.
He was late, therefore he missed the bus.
questions.explanation: A semicolon joins two independent clauses, with a comma after 'therefore'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Punctuate correctly: what a beautiful sunset exclaimed the tourist
questions.answer: 'What a beautiful sunset!' exclaimed the tourist.
keyPoints: exclamation mark inside the inverted commas
questions.explanation: The exclamation stays inside the quotation marks.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Give one use of the semicolon, with an example.
questions.answer: A semicolon joins two closely related independent clauses: She was tired; she went to bed early.
questions.explanation: A semicolon is stronger than a comma but weaker than a full stop.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the synonym of 'assist'.
questions.explanation: 'Assist' means to help.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'expand'.
questions.explanation: To expand is to become larger; to shrink is to become smaller.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: A collection of poems or other literary pieces is called a(n)
questions.explanation: An anthology is a collection of selected writings.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Accommodation' has double c and double m.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: The suffix -able in 'readable' means
questions.explanation: Readable means capable of being read.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: If an argument is 'cogent', it is
questions.explanation: A cogent argument is clear, logical and convincing.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Write the opposites of 'increase', 'accept' and 'polite'.
questions.explanation: Antonyms have opposite meanings.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the difference between 'stationary' and 'stationery'.
questions.answer: 'Stationary' means not moving. 'Stationery' means writing materials such as pens and paper.
questions.explanation: The words sound alike but are spelt and used differently.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'to pull someone's leg' mean?
questions.explanation: It means to joke with or tease someone.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'at the eleventh hour' mean?
questions.explanation: It means at the last possible moment.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'to keep an eye on' mean?
questions.explanation: It means to watch something or someone carefully.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'to beat around the bush' mean?
options: to avoid coming to the point
questions.explanation: It means to talk about unimportant matters instead of the main point.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the phrasal verb 'turn down' mean in 'She turned down the offer'?
questions.explanation: 'Turn down' means to refuse.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: The company decided to ___ a new branch in Surat.
questions.explanation: 'Set up' means to establish something.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the idiom 'a storm in a teacup' and use it in a sentence.
questions.answer: It means a lot of fuss about something unimportant: The argument over the seat was a storm in a teacup.
keyPoints: means excitement over a trivial matter
questions.explanation: The idiom describes a small problem treated as a big one.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the phrasal verb 'break down' and use it in a sentence.
questions.answer: 'Break down' means to stop working (of a machine): Our car broke down on the highway.
keyPoints: means to stop working or fail
questions.explanation: It is commonly used for vehicles and machines.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Kabir's father repairs bicycles in a tiny shop near the bus stand. Kabir often helps him after school by pumping air into tyres. What does Kabir's father do?
questions.explanation: He repairs bicycles in a tiny shop.

How does Kabir help his father?
questions.explanation: The passage says he pumps air into tyres after school.

What does Kabir's plan show?
options: He respects his father's work and wants to carry it forward
He wants to leave the town
He thinks the shop earns too much
questions.explanation: He wants to grow the same trade and teach others.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Kabir's father repairs bicycles in a tiny shop near the bus stand. Kabir often helps him after school by pumping air into tyres. What does Kabir's father believe about honest work?
questions.answer: He believes that honest work is its own reward, even if it earns little money.
keyPoints: honest work is its own reward
money earned is not the only measure
questions.explanation: The passage quotes this belief.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Sound travels in waves. These waves move through air, water and solids, but they cannot travel through empty space because there is nothing to carry them. questions.explanation: The passage lists air, water and solids.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Sound travels in waves. These waves move through air, water and solids, but they cannot travel through empty space because there is nothing to carry them. options: There is nothing to carry the waves
questions.explanation: The passage says there is nothing to carry the waves.

questions.subject: english

This is why astronauts working outside a spacecraft cannot hear each other without radios.' What does the example of the astronauts show?
options: Sound needs a material to travel through, which space lacks

This is why astronauts working outside a spacecraft cannot hear each other without radios.' Why do astronauts need radios to talk outside their spacecraft?
questions.answer: Outside the spacecraft there is empty space with nothing to carry sound waves, so they cannot hear each other without radios.
keyPoints: sound waves need something to travel through
questions.explanation: The passage gives this cause directly.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Neha found a wallet on the pavement outside the market. Inside were some money and a card with an address. options: On the pavement outside the market
questions.explanation: She found it on the pavement outside the market.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Neha found a wallet on the pavement outside the market. Inside were some money and a card with an address. Though she was tempted to keep the money for a new book, she remembered how worried her mother had been when she once lost her purse. She walked three streets to the address and returned the wallet to its grateful owner.' What helped Neha decide to return the wallet?
options: She remembered her mother's worry when she lost a purse
She did not need a book
questions.explanation: The memory of her mother's worry changed her mind.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Neha found a wallet on the pavement outside the market. Inside were some money and a card with an address. Though she was tempted to keep the money for a new book, she remembered how worried her mother had been when she once lost her purse. She walked three streets to the address and returned the wallet to its grateful owner.' In the passage, 'tempted' means

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'Neha found a wallet on the pavement outside the market. Inside were some money and a card with an address. Though she was tempted to keep the money for a new book, she remembered how worried her mother had been when she once lost her purse. questions.explanation: Her choices show honesty and empathy.

questions.subject: english

questions.explanation: The first sentence states this.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'A rainbow appears when sunlight passes through raindrops. The drops bend and split the light into its colours, which spread out in a curved band. To see a rainbow, you must stand with the sun behind you and the raindrops in front of you.' Where must you stand to see a rainbow?
options: With the sun behind you and the rain in front
questions.explanation: The last sentence gives this position.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'A rainbow appears when sunlight passes through raindrops. The drops bend and split the light into its colours, which spread out in a curved band. To see a rainbow, you must stand with the sun behind you and the raindrops in front of you.' What do raindrops do to sunlight?
options: Bend and split it into colours
questions.explanation: The drops bend and split the light into its colours.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Read the passage. 'A rainbow appears when sunlight passes through raindrops. The drops bend and split the light into its colours, which spread out in a curved band. To see a rainbow, you must stand with the sun behind you and the raindrops in front of you.' Explain how a rainbow is formed.
questions.answer: Sunlight passes through raindrops, which bend and split it into its colours; the colours spread out as a curved band.
keyPoints: drops bend and split the light into colours
questions.explanation: The passage describes the steps.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The earth ___ round the sun.
questions.explanation: A scientific fact takes the simple present, with -s for a singular subject.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: At 8 p.m. yesterday, we ___ dinner.
questions.explanation: An action in progress at a stated past time takes the past continuous.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: She ___ in Mysuru for three years before she moved to Kolkata.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past events takes the past perfect: had lived.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: I ___ my keys; can you help me look for them?
questions.explanation: A past action with a present result is expressed by the present perfect.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: He ___ to the gym every day, but today he is resting.
questions.explanation: A daily habit takes the simple present.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: I am working here since March.
We have known each other for years.
questions.explanation: 'Know' is a state verb used in the present perfect with 'for'; the other sentences misuse tense.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into the simple future tense: 'They visited the museum.'
questions.explanation: The simple future is formed with will and the base form.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Correct the error: 'I have met him yesterday.'
questions.explanation: The present perfect cannot be used with a finished time expression.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The students ___ in the library.
questions.explanation: 'Students' is plural, so the verb is 'are'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: She ___ a beautiful voice.
questions.explanation: A singular subject takes 'has'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The teacher, together with the students, ___ gone on a trip.
questions.explanation: 'Together with' does not make the subject plural; the verb agrees with 'teacher'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Half of the cake ___ eaten.
questions.explanation: 'Cake' is singular, so the verb is singular.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Measles ___ a contagious disease.
questions.explanation: 'Measles' ends in -s but is a singular name of a disease.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Each of the boys have a bat.
A number of reasons was given.
Every boy and every girl was given a certificate.
questions.explanation: Subjects joined by 'and' but each preceded by 'every' are treated as singular.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Correct the error: 'My trousers is too long.'
questions.explanation: Trousers, like scissors, is always plural in grammar.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Rewrite correctly: 'Neither the principal nor the teachers was present.'
questions.answer: Neither the principal nor the teachers were present.
keyPoints: with neither ... nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the subject closer to it.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct article: He is ___ MLA.
questions.explanation: 'MLA' is pronounced 'em-el-ay', which begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct article: She wore ___ red saree.
questions.explanation: 'Red' begins with a consonant sound, so 'a' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct article: He plays ___ guitar very well.
questions.explanation: 'The' is used with musical instruments after 'play'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ of my friends lives in Delhi.
questions.explanation: 'One of' is followed by a plural noun and a singular verb, which matches 'lives'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: How ___ rice do you need for the recipe?
questions.explanation: 'Rice' is uncountable, so 'much' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: He has a one-year-old son and an one-rupee coin.
She visited an orphanage on Sunday.
questions.explanation: 'Orphanage' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is correct; the other sentences use the wrong article.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Fill in with a, an or the: 'She asked for ___ apple and ___ orange. ___ apple was sweet.'
keyPoints: the for the apple already mentioned
questions.explanation: The first mentions are indefinite; the second mention of the apple is definite.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain why 'school' has no article in 'He went to school' but has one in 'He went to the school to meet the principal'.
questions.answer: Without 'the', school refers to the purpose of the place, studying. With 'the', it refers to a particular school building he visited for another reason.
keyPoints: no article: the institution and its purpose
questions.explanation: The article shows whether we speak of an activity or a specific place.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: He was born ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: 'On' is used with days of the week.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: The shop opens ___ nine o'clock.
questions.explanation: 'At' is used with clock times.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: She is proud ___ her son.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'proud' is followed by 'of'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: He is suffering ___ fever.
questions.explanation: The verb 'suffer' takes 'from' with an illness.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: Work hard, ___ you will fail.
questions.explanation: 'Or' means 'otherwise' and joins a command to the result of not following it.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: He congratulated me for my success.
He congratulated me on my success.
He congratulated me at my success.
He congratulated me with my success.
questions.explanation: 'Congratulate' is followed by 'on'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Join using 'as soon as': 'He saw the snake. He ran away.'
questions.answer: As soon as he saw the snake, he ran away.
keyPoints: as soon as shows immediate sequence
questions.explanation: 'As soon as' joins two actions that follow each other immediately.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Fill in the blanks with prepositions: 'She is good ___ music and keen ___ learning the sitar.'
questions.explanation: These adjectives take fixed prepositions.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ not swim, so I stayed on the shore.
questions.explanation: 'Could not' expresses inability in the past.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ you please open the window?
questions.explanation: 'Could you please...?' is a polite request.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: Take your raincoat; it ___ rain this afternoon.
questions.explanation: 'Might' expresses a possibility.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ we go for a walk after dinner?
questions.explanation: 'Shall we...?' is used to make a suggestion.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct word: Visitors ___ not feed the animals.
questions.explanation: 'Must not' expresses prohibition.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence gives advice?
questions.explanation: 'Should' is used for advice.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Rewrite using 'should': 'It is advisable to save some money every month.'
questions.answer: You should save some money every month.
keyPoints: base form of the verb follows
questions.explanation: 'Should' gives advice or says what is a good idea.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the difference in meaning between 'He should have come' and 'He must have come'.
questions.answer: 'He should have come' means it was his duty to come, but he did not. 'He must have come' means I conclude that he came.
keyPoints: must have = logical conclusion about the past
questions.explanation: Modal + have + past participle can express regret or deduction.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The door ___ by the watchman.
questions.explanation: The door receives the action, so the passive 'was opened' is used.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Rice ___ in many parts of India.
questions.explanation: A general fact in the passive: is grown.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'She was singing a song.'
options: A song was sung by her.
A song was being sung by her.
A song is being sung by her.
A song had been sung by her.
questions.explanation: Past continuous active becomes was/were being + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'They will build a dam.'
options: A dam is built by them.
A dam would be built by them.
A dam will built by them.
A dam will be built by them.
questions.explanation: Simple future passive: will be + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'The boy has eaten the apple.'
options: The apple has been eaten by the boy.
The apple was eaten by the boy.
The apple is eaten by the boy.
The apple had been eaten by the boy.
questions.explanation: Present perfect active becomes has/have been + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: The tap was fixed by Rahul.
questions.explanation: In the passive the subject (tap) receives the action.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into the passive voice: 'The children sang the national anthem.'
questions.answer: The national anthem was sung by the children.
questions.explanation: Simple past passive: was + past participle.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into the active voice: 'The prizes will be distributed by the Chief Guest.'
questions.answer: The Chief Guest will distribute the prizes.
keyPoints: will be distributed becomes will distribute
questions.explanation: Remove 'be + past participle' and use the base verb after will.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I play football.'
options: He said that he played football.
He said that I played football.
He said that he will play football.
He said that he had play football.
questions.explanation: The simple present becomes the simple past and 'I' becomes 'he'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: They said, 'We are winning.'
options: They said that we were winning.
They said that they would be winning.
They said that they were winning.
They said that they have been winning.
questions.explanation: 'We' becomes 'they' and the present continuous becomes the past continuous.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said, 'I saw him yesterday.'
options: She said that she had seen him tomorrow.
She said that I had seen him the day before.
She said that she has seen him the day before.
She said that she had seen him the day before.
questions.explanation: Simple past becomes past perfect and 'yesterday' becomes 'the day before'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He asked, 'Can you swim?'
options: He asked me that I could swim.
He asked me if I could swim.
He asked me could I swim.
He asked me what I could swim.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with 'if', and 'can' becomes 'could'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: The teacher said to the student, 'Work hard.'
options: The teacher said the student work hard.
The teacher advised the student that work hard.
The teacher advised the student to work hard.
The teacher asked the student if he worked hard.
questions.explanation: A command or advice is reported with 'advised ... to + verb'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: Mother said to me, 'May God bless you!'
options: Mother prayed that God might bless me.
Mother said that God may bless me.
Mother asked God to bless her.
Mother prayed that God bless me.
questions.explanation: A blessing or wish is reported with 'prayed that' and 'might'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, 'Where are you going?'
questions.answer: He asked me where I was going.
questions.explanation: A wh-question is reported with the same question word.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into direct speech: The mother told her son not to play near the road.
questions.answer: The mother said to her son, 'Do not play near the road.'
questions.explanation: A reported negative command becomes a direct 'Do not...' sentence.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: The part of a sentence that says something about the subject is called the
questions.explanation: The predicate tells what the subject does or is.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Combine using 'both ... and': 'He is honest. He is hardworking.'
options: He is both honest or hardworking.
Both he is honest and hardworking.
He both is honest and hardworking.
He is both honest and hardworking.
questions.explanation: 'Both' and 'and' must come directly before the two words joined.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Rewrite using 'unless': 'If you do not work hard, you will fail.'
options: Unless you do not work hard, you will fail.
Unless you worked hard, you will fail.
Unless you work hard, you will not fail.
Unless you work hard, you will fail.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not', so the verb after it is positive.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into a simple sentence: 'He went to the market so that he might buy fruit.'
options: He went to the market for buy fruit.
He went to the market to buy fruit.
He went to the market for to buy fruit.
He went to the market and buy fruit.
questions.explanation: A clause of purpose can be shortened to 'to + verb'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into the superlative degree: 'Gold is more precious than any other metal.'
options: Gold is the more precious metal.
Gold is the most precious metal.
Gold is the precious metal most.
questions.explanation: The superlative uses 'the most + adjective'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: In 'He stayed at home because he was ill', the clause 'because he was ill' is a/an
questions.explanation: It tells why he stayed at home, so it is an adverb clause of reason.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Change into an exclamatory sentence: 'The sky is very blue.'
questions.explanation: 'How + adjective' forms an exclamation.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Combine using 'not only ... but also': 'She sings well. She dances well.'
questions.answer: She not only sings well but also dances well.
keyPoints: not only before the first verb phrase
questions.explanation: The pair joins two parallel parts of the sentence.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which punctuation mark is used to show possession?
questions.explanation: The apostrophe shows that something belongs to someone.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which words need capital letters in: 'on monday we visited the red fort.'?
questions.explanation: The first word of the sentence and the names of a day and a monument begin with capitals.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
questions.explanation: A comma follows the introductory word 'Yes'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: A comma follows each part of the split quotation before and after the speaker tag.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence uses the colon correctly?
options: The shop sells three things: books, pens and bags.
The shop sells three things; books, pens and bags.
The shop sells; three things, books pens and bags.
The shop sells three things, books: pens and bags.
questions.explanation: A colon after a complete statement introduces a list.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: Its a lovely day, isn't it
It's a lovely day isn't it?
It's a lovely day, isn't it?
Its a lovely day, isnt it?
questions.explanation: It's has an apostrophe, a comma sets off the tag question, and the sentence ends with a question mark.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Punctuate correctly: rohan said i am going to delhi on friday
questions.answer: Rohan said, 'I am going to Delhi on Friday.'
keyPoints: capital letters for names and days
questions.explanation: Direct speech is placed in inverted commas after a comma.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Why does 'the girls' room' take an apostrophe but 'the girls play' does not?
questions.answer: In 'the girls' room' the apostrophe shows possession (the room belongs to the girls). In 'the girls play' the -s only makes 'girl' plural, so no apostrophe is needed.
questions.explanation: Plurals and possessives are different things.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the synonym of 'courage'.
questions.explanation: Courage and bravery have the same meaning.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'victory'.
questions.explanation: 'Defeat' is the opposite of 'victory'.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: A person who has just started learning something is called a
questions.explanation: A novice is a beginner.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The rule is 'i before e except after c', so receive.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: The prefix 'un-' in 'unhappy' means
questions.explanation: 'Un-' gives the opposite meaning: not happy.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Something that is 'ephemeral' is
questions.explanation: 'Ephemeral' means short-lived.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Form verbs from the words 'beauty', 'strength' and 'class'.
questions.explanation: Suffixes such as -ify and -en turn nouns into verbs.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: Explain the difference between 'complement' and 'compliment', with a sentence for each.
questions.answer: 'Complement' means something that completes or goes well with another: The scarf complements her dress. 'Compliment' means an expression of praise: He paid her a compliment.
questions.explanation: The words sound alike but have different meanings.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'to face the music' mean?
options: to accept the consequences of one's actions
questions.explanation: It means to accept the unpleasant results of what one has done.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'a drop in the ocean' mean?
options: a very small amount compared with what is needed
questions.explanation: It describes something too small to make much difference.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'to hit the sack' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Hit the sack' is an informal way of saying to go to bed.

questions.subject: english
questions.q: What does the idiom 'out of the blue' mean?
questions.explanation: It means suddenly and without warning.
